subject: SLA carveout request — customer-controlled network and latency tail (Kapstone)
messages:
From: Riley Chen <riley.chen@kapstone.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@kapstone.ai>, Markus Liao <m.liao@kapstone.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment SLA question — latency tail and egress responsibilities

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo — Kapstone's infra team has a couple of follow-ups as we finalize the SOW. We're planning to run Redwood Private in our colo-fed VPC (customer-managed routers and transit fabric). The main ask from ops is that any uptime/latency commitments exclude impacts caused by our edge network (outside of the VM/eBPF tunnel endpoint). Specifically:

- We see intermittent 99.99->99.90 drops during scheduled maintenance windows on our transit provider; we'd like those to be carved out of Redwood's latency/availability SLOs.
- For p95/p99 latency guarantees, we want a clause that removes responsibility for network jitter and packet loss from our side (from our router egress onward).

I've attached a network diagram and a short ops control matrix. Can Redwood produce a redline or exception statement we can share with our legal team?

Appreciate it — Riley
Infrastructure Lead, Kapstone Analytics

Attachments: kapstone_network_diagram.pdf, kapstone_ops_control_matrix.xlsx

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Riley Chen <riley.chen@kapstone.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA question — latency tail and egress responsibilities

Riley — thanks for the clear writeup and the diagrams. Short answer: we can accommodate carveouts for customer-controlled network layers, but we need explicit language that defines the demarcation point and how latency measurements are performed.

Proposed next steps:
- Ben (commercial/legal) will draft an exception appendix with a demarcation diagram and measurement points (ingress/egress).
- Neha will confirm how Redwood's monitoring instrumentation reports p95/p99 when signals cross the egress point.
- We'll propose fallback behavior (automatic model failover to hosted variants) and any cost/throughput implications.

Ben/Neha — please review the attached ops matrix and suggest redline language.

—Tessa
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 08:57:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft exception language (first pass)

Team — first pass below. I've kept it narrow to the network demarcation and measurement method so it can be signed quickly: 

1) Demarcation: "Customer Network Demarcation Point" shall be the egress interface of the customer's primary transit router, defined in the appendix by IP/netblock and the provided network diagram. Redwood's obligations for latency and availability SLOs apply only to requests that are received by Redwood's designated ingress endpoint.

2) Measurement: Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) will be calculated at Redwood's ingress and egress probes. Any packet loss, jitter, or path instability measured solely within the Customer Network Demarcation Point or downstream transit providers will be excluded from Redwood availability and latency calculations.

3) Failover and remediation: For requests that exceed configured latency thresholds attributable to Customer Network, Redwood will offer automatic model routing to the nearest hosted region (if enabled by the customer) and operational runbooks for joint troubleshooting. Redwood will not be responsible for costs incurred by the customer's transit provider.

4) Liability cap: No change to the overall SLAs' financial caps; exceptions apply only to measurement and remediation obligations.

This is intentionally conservative; happy to iterate. Neha — can you confirm whether our probe locations and logging capture the egress-side timestamps we need?

Ben
Sr. Commercial Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 12:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft exception language (first pass)

Ben — we have ingress and egress probes in the customer's region and can instrument an egress-side timestamp at Redwood's border. Two practical notes: 

- For precise attribution we will need the customer's assistance to provide mirroring or passive flow logs for at least a 30-day baseline. Without that, attribution windows will rely on correlation heuristics (which are usually fine for operational purposes but weaker for legal disputes).
- Our monitoring currently uses the request arrival time at the edge LB as the canonical latency start — we'll add a labeled probe for "customer-demarcation-timestamp" so both sides can reconcile measurements.

I'll draft a short SRE runbook clause for inclusion that covers instrumentation, evidence collection, and SLA dispute resolution timelines.

Neha
Head of SRE Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Liao <m.liao@kapstone.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Riley Chen <riley.chen@kapstone.ai>, Asha Patel <asha.patel@kapstone.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Kapstone redlines — request for explicit exclusion and auditability

Tessa/Ben — thanks. Kapstone legal has two edits: 

A) Wording: we want an explicit exclusion clause that states "Redwood's availability and latency guarantees shall not apply to failures or degradations caused by Customer-controlled network infrastructure, including but not limited to transit provider outages, edge router misconfiguration, or third-party CDN misuse, where responsibility is traceable to Customer or Customer vendors."

B) Auditability: we need a binding commitment to provide retained logs and a 30-day window for joint inspection in the event of a claim. Please confirm retention format and access method.

If Redwood can accept both items, Kapstone can greenlight signature from procurement.

Regards, Markus
Senior Counsel, Kapstone Analytics

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Markus Liao <m.liao@kapstone.ai>, Riley Chen <riley.chen@kapstone.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kapstone redlines — request for explicit exclusion and auditability

Markus/Riley — quick confirmation after internal review: Redwood can accept the explicit exclusion language with a clarifying sentence that defines the demarcation (we'll append the IP/netblock and the diagram). On auditability: Redwood will provide access to request-level logs and probe traces for a 30-day window accessible via a secured shared bucket and a signed NDA for forensic review. We'll include an SRE-led dispute process: 5 business days to provide initial evidence, 20 business days for joint analysis, and escalation to legal if unresolved.

Attached is our draft exception appendix (draft-sla-exception-amendment-20280621.docx) with the demarcation diagram and the runbook. If that looks good, Ben will route the final redline to your procurement.

—Tessa
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachments: draft-sla-exception-amendment-20280621.docx
